How to sew a lined tote bag with boxed corners

A lined tote with long straps: one piece of cotton duck, one of satin, two straps. Watch it come together step by step.

Overview

The finished bag

A lined tote in three parts: a cotton duck outer, a satin lining and two long straps. Tap the bag to take it apart.

  1. 1Outer — cotton duck · cut 86 × 45 cm (33⅞ × 17¾ in), folded at the bottom
  2. 2Lining — satin · cut 86 × 45 cm, the same as the outer
  3. 3Straps ×2 — cut 100 × 16 cm (39⅜ × 6¼ in) · folded in four to 4 cm (1⅝ in)
  4. 4Bottom — two folds stitched 6 cm (2⅜ in) each side of the centre crease, tucked in before the side seams → a 12 cm (4¾ in) base, the corners form by themselves
  5. 5Topstitch — 1 cm (⅜ in) from the top edge · all seams 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in)

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Cut one 86 × 45 cm (33⅞ × 17¾ in) rectangle of cotton duck for the outer and one of satin, the same size, for the lining.

    For the straps, cut two strips of duck, 100 × 16 cm (39⅜ × 6¼ in).

    On the outer and the lining, mark the fold line across the middle, 43 cm (16⅞ in) from either short end — it becomes the bottom of the bag.

    Every seam allowance in this bag is 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in).

  2. Fold a strip in half lengthwise, wrong sides together, and press a crease.

    Open it out. Fold both long edges in so they meet at the crease, and press again.

    Fold in half along the first crease. The strap is now 4 cm (1⅝ in) wide and four layers thick, with every raw edge tucked inside.

    Topstitch close to both long edges with a straight stitch. Make two straps.

    Machine: straight stitch

  3. Fold the outer in half across the middle and press a crease. Open it out again.

    Measure 6 cm (2⅜ in) from the crease towards each end and mark a line across the whole width of the piece.

    Fold along the first line, right sides together, and stitch close to the fold. Open it out, then fold and stitch along the second line the same way.

    The two stitched folds, 12 cm (4¾ in) apart, are the edges of the bottom; the centre crease is its middle.

    Machine: straight stitch

  4. Lay the piece right side up and lift both ends, so it bends at the two stitched folds.

    Bring the ends together. The 12 cm (4¾ in) bottom folds in on itself and the centre crease goes inside, 6 cm (2⅜ in) up between the layers — like the bottom of a paper bag.

    Lay it flat, right sides together. The stitched folds are now the bottom edge, and the folded piece is 6 cm shorter than a plain fold in half.

  5. Clip the sides so the tucked-in bottom stays in place.

    Sew both side seams, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge, all the way down. At the bottom the seam goes through four layers — the front, the two halves of the tucked bottom and the back. Leave the top open.

    Machine: straight stitch

  6. Turn the outer right side out through the top.

    Open it up and push the bottom out. The tucked bottom unfolds into a flat 12 cm (4¾ in) base, and where the side seams caught it, neat corners form by themselves — no extra corner seams needed.

  7. Make the lining exactly like the outer: crease the centre, stitch the two folds 6 cm (2⅜ in) from it, tuck the bottom in.

    Sew both side seams, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge — but on one side leave an 8 cm (3⅛ in) gap, low down just above the tucked bottom. You will turn the bag through it.

    Keep the lining inside out.

    Machine: straight stitch

  8. Turn the outer right side out.

    Pin a strap to the front top edge: ends level with the raw edge, 6 cm (2⅜ in) from the centre, the loop hanging down over the bag. Do the same on the back.

    Slip the outer, straps and all, into the inside-out lining, so the right sides face each other. Line up the side seams and the top edges.

    Sew all the way around the top, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge.

    Machine: straight stitch

  9. Pull the whole bag right side out through the opening in the lining.

    Tuck in the raw edges of the opening and stitch it closed, close to the edge.

    Push the lining down inside the bag and press the top edge flat.

    Topstitch all around the top, 1 cm (⅜ in) from the edge. Your tote is done!

    Machine: straight stitch

Good to know

Questions and answers

How much fabric do I need for a tote bag?

For this tote you cut four pieces: an 86 × 45 cm (33⅞ × 17¾ in) rectangle of cotton duck for the outer, a satin one the same size for the lining, and two duck strips 100 × 16 cm (39⅜ × 6¼ in) for the straps. The cutting diagram below shows them all.

How do you make the bottom and boxed corners of a tote bag?

This tote needs no separate corner seams. Crease the outer across the middle, fold 6 cm (2⅜ in) to each side of the crease and stitch close to each fold. Tuck the bottom in so the crease goes 6 cm inside, then sew the side seams through all the layers. Turn it out: the bottom opens into a 12 cm (4¾ in) base and the corners form by themselves. The lining is made the same way.

Does a tote bag need a lining?

Not every tote has one, but this one does: satin, cut the same size as the outer, 86 × 45 cm, and sewn the same way, with an 8 cm (3⅛ in) opening left in one side seam. It covers the seams inside the bag. There is no interfacing.

What seam allowance should I use for a tote bag?

Every seam in this tote is 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in): the side seams of the outer and the lining and the seam around the top. The topstitching around the top goes 1 cm (⅜ in) from the edge.

Where do you leave the opening to turn a lined bag?

In one side seam of the lining, low down just above the tucked-in bottom: leave 8 cm (3⅛ in) unsewn. Turn the whole bag right side out through it, then tuck in the raw edges and stitch the opening closed, close to the edge.

How long should tote bag straps be?

For this tote, cut two strips 100 × 16 cm (39⅜ × 6¼ in). Fold each into four layers — in half, open, both edges to the crease, in half again — for a 4 cm (1⅝ in) strap, and topstitch both edges. Pin the ends level with the top edge, 6 cm (2⅜ in) from the centre.
